ADaM Module

Source: vignettes/adam-module.Rmd
adam-module.Rmd

Overview

This vignette demonstrates the bundled ADaM module — a set of conformance checks for ADaM datasets (ADSL and BDS) that ship with the core aRtifacts package.

Companion package roadmap: These ADaM-specific helpers are bundled in the core today and will eventually move to a dedicated aRtifacts.adam companion package.

The checks are aligned with key concepts from the ADaM Implementation Guide (ADaMIG) v1.3: required variables, key uniqueness, population flags, parameter naming, treatment variables, and baseline derivation rules.

Step 1 — Inspect the example datasets

aRtifacts ships with two small synthetic ADaM datasets you can use for demos and testing.

ADSL — one row per subject 

library(aRtifacts)

adsl <- example_adsl()
adsl
#>   STUDYID     USUBJID SUBJID SITEID AGE  AGEU SEX  RACE     ARM  TRT01P SAFFL
#> 1 STUDY01 STUDY01-001    001 SITE01  63 YEARS   F WHITE  Drug A  Drug A     Y
#> 2 STUDY01 STUDY01-002    002 SITE01  58 YEARS   M WHITE  Drug A  Drug A     Y
#> 3 STUDY01 STUDY01-003    003 SITE02  71 YEARS   F ASIAN Placebo Placebo     Y
#>   FASFL
#> 1     Y
#> 2     Y
#> 3     N

Three subjects across two sites. Notice FASFL = "N" for subject 003 — that’s intentional and valid (population flags must be Y or N, never missing).

ADVS (BDS) — one or more rows per subject × parameter × timepoint 

advs <- example_advs()
advs
#>   STUDYID     USUBJID                          PARAM PARAMCD AVAL   AVISIT ADY
#> 1 STUDY01 STUDY01-001 Systolic Blood Pressure (mmHg)   SYSBP  130 BASELINE   1
#> 2 STUDY01 STUDY01-001 Systolic Blood Pressure (mmHg)   SYSBP  122   WEEK 4  29
#> 3 STUDY01 STUDY01-002 Systolic Blood Pressure (mmHg)   SYSBP  140 BASELINE   1
#> 4 STUDY01 STUDY01-002 Systolic Blood Pressure (mmHg)   SYSBP  136   WEEK 4  29
#> 5 STUDY01 STUDY01-003 Systolic Blood Pressure (mmHg)   SYSBP  150 BASELINE   1
#>      TRTP ABLFL BASE CHG
#> 1  Drug A     Y  130   0
#> 2  Drug A  <NA>  130  -8
#> 3  Drug A     Y  140   0
#> 4  Drug A  <NA>  140  -4
#> 5 Placebo     Y  150   0

Five rows of systolic blood pressure. Subjects 001 and 002 have both BASELINE and WEEK 4 visits; subject 003 has only BASELINE. The ABLFL column marks which record is the baseline record for each subject (Y at baseline, NA at post-baseline).

Step 2 — Run ADSL checks

check_adsl() verifies the structural expectations of a subject-level analysis dataset:

  • Required variables — STUDYID, USUBJID, SUBJID, SITEID, AGE, AGEU, SEX, RACE, ARM, TRT01P
  • USUBJID uniqueness — every subject should appear exactly once
  • Population flags — at least one *FL variable, with values restricted to Y/N
adsl_issues <- check_adsl(adsl)
adsl_issues
#> [1] check    severity message  n       
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

Reading the output: An empty (zero-row) issue table means the dataset passed all checks. Each row that does appear tells you:

Column Meaning
check Which rule fired (e.g., ADSL_REQUIRED, ADSL_USUBJID_UNIQUE)
severity error = must fix, warning = should investigate
message Human-readable explanation
n How many records or variables are affected (NA if not applicable)

Step 3 — Run BDS checks

check_bds() covers the basic data structure expectations:

  • Required variables — STUDYID, USUBJID, PARAM, PARAMCD
  • Analysis value — at least one of AVAL or AVALC must exist
  • Treatment variable — expects TRT01P, TRTP, or TRTA
  • PARAM ↔︎ PARAMCD mapping — must be one-to-one
  • PARAMCD format — ≤ 8 characters, starts with a letter
  • Relative timing — when multiple records per subject×parameter exist, a timing variable (ADY, AVISIT, etc.) should be present
  • Baseline derivation — if BASE is populated, ABLFL must exist and every subject×parameter with a non-null BASE must have at least one ABLFL = "Y" record
bds_issues <- check_bds(advs)
bds_issues
#> [1] check    severity message  n       
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

Again, an empty table means everything passed. If you see rows, the check column tells you exactly which ADaMIG concept was violated.

Step 4 — Validate everything in one call

validate_adam() is a convenience wrapper that runs both check_adsl() and check_bds() and returns a structured list. You can pass a single BDS dataset or a named list of multiple BDS datasets.

results <- validate_adam(
  adsl = adsl,
  bds  = list(ADVS = advs)
)

results$adsl
#> [1] check    severity message  n       
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
results$bds$ADVS
#> [1] check    severity message  n       
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

The output is a nested list — $adsl for the ADSL issue table, $bds for a named list of BDS issue tables (one per dataset). This structure makes it easy to iterate programmatically or pipe into a reporting template.

Step 5 — Combine with the core engine

The ADaM module works alongside the core snapshot/diff/rule engine. Here’s a typical end-to-end flow:

  1. Snapshot your ADVS at two data cuts.
  2. Diff them to see what changed.
  3. Run flags to catch clinical-review issues.
  4. Run check_bds() to verify ADaMIG conformance.
# Two data cuts
advs_v1 <- advs
advs_v2 <- advs
advs_v2$AVAL[advs_v2$USUBJID == "STUDY01-002" & advs_v2$AVISIT == "WEEK 4"] <- 195

snap_v1 <- new_domain_snapshot("ADVS", advs_v1, key_vars = c("USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVISIT"))
snap_v2 <- new_domain_snapshot("ADVS", advs_v2, key_vars = c("USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVISIT"))

What changed? 

diff_values(snap_v1, snap_v2, vars = "AVAL")
#>       USUBJID PARAMCD AVISIT  var old new
#> 4 STUDY01-002   SYSBP WEEK 4 AVAL 136 195

Subject 002’s WEEK 4 systolic BP jumped from 136 → 195. That’s a large single-visit change and might warrant clinical review.

Flag it with a custom rule 

art_v2 <- new_artifact_snapshot(domains = list(ADVS = snap_v2), build_id = "cut-2")

rule_high_bp <- new_flag_rule(
  id         = "HIGH_SYSBP",
  domain     = "ADVS",
  severity   = "warning",
  category   = "clinical_review",
  owner_team = "Medical Monitor",
  fn = function(df) {
    out <- df[df$PARAMCD == "SYSBP" & !is.na(df$AVAL) & df$AVAL > 180, , drop = FALSE]
    if (!nrow(out)) return(data.frame())
    out[, c("USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVISIT", "AVAL"), drop = FALSE]
  }
)

run_flags(art_v2, list(rule_high_bp))
#>       USUBJID PARAMCD AVISIT AVAL    RULE_ID DOMAIN SEVERITY        CATEGORY
#> 4 STUDY01-002   SYSBP WEEK 4  195 HIGH_SYSBP   ADVS  warning clinical_review
#>        OWNER_TEAM
#> 4 Medical Monitor

The flag identifies subject 002 at WEEK 4 with a systolic BP of 195. The OWNER_TEAM column tells you who should investigate.

Confirm ADaMIG conformance 

check_bds(advs_v2)
#> [1] check    severity message  n       
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

No structural issues — the dataset is still ADaMIG-compliant even with the clinically notable value.
